title: Policy Learning with Network-Shaping Assignments
abstract: arXiv:2610.29221v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Many policies determine social arrangements whose effects depend on the relationships formed afterwards. We study how to learn such policies when a constrained joint action changes network formation and outcomes depend on exposures to the resulting network. Policy value integrates an outcome response over the distribution of post-assignment networks. The large number of feasible arrangements makes it difficult to evaluate policies directly from historical data. We therefore adopt a model-based approach that pools information across assignments to evaluate alternative arrangements. We characterize identification of policy values and construct plug-in estimators. Our regret bounds account for sampling variation, first-stage estimation error, and computational errors. Our applications to classroom seating and business groups illustrate predicted welfare gains from learned rules relative to random assignment.

translated_title: 基于网络塑造型分配的策略学习
translated_abstract: 许多政策决定了社会安排，其效果取决于随后形成的人际关系。我们研究当受约束的联合行动会改变网络形成、且结果依赖于由此产生网络的暴露效应时，如何学习此类政策。政策价值是对分配后网络分布上的结果响应进行积分。由于可行安排的数量庞大，直接从历史数据评估政策十分困难。因此，我们采用一种基于模型的方法，汇集跨分配的信息来评估各种替代安排。我们刻画了政策价值的可识别性，并构建了即插即用估计量。我们的遗憾界考虑了抽样变异、第一阶段估计误差以及计算误差。在课堂座位安排和商业团体上的应用表明，学习到的规则相对于随机分配能够带来预测的福利收益。
tldr: 本文研究学习能够塑造网络形成的政策分配问题，通过基于模型的方法刻画政策价值的可识别性并构建带遗憾界保证的即插即用估计量，在课堂座位和商业团体应用中显示学习到的规则相比随机分配可带来福利提升。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a model-based policy learning approach for assignments that shape network formation, characterizes identification of policy values, constructs plug-in estimators with regret bounds accounting for sampling, estimation, and computational errors, and demonstrates welfare gains over random assignment in classroom seating and business group applications.
